title: The Ring of Fire
logline: At a night procession, a fire performer whirls a torch and the crowd sees a ring of fire. Up close there is only one flame, a pair of hands, and years of practice.

object.note: Object 1 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The question of how much we 'know' through the senses moves from the tongue to the eye: at night, a single flame that a crowd sees as a ring.

thread_out.thread: From a procession's fire to a neighbourhood's paper lights: something built with great care, seen for a few nights, then taken apart.
